1	// Shared fixtures for the POST /groups/:id/import suites.
2	import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
3	import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
4	import { dirname } from 'node:path'
5	import { startApp, tempDataFile } from './helpers.mjs'
6	
7	export const trip = { id: 'trip', name: 'Ski trip', members: ['Ann', 'Ben', 'Cara'] }
8	
9	// Import entries; fields override the defaults.
10	export const expense = (fields = {}) => ({ type: 'expense', description: 'Hotel', payer: 'Ann', amount: 90, ...fields })
11	export const payment = (fields = {}) => ({ type: 'payment', from: 'Ben', to: 'Ann', amount: 30, ...fields })
12	
13	// The same expense as a body for POST /groups/:id/expenses (no type).
14	export const expenseBody = (fields = {}) => {
15	  const { type, ...body } = expense(fields)
16	  return body
17	}
18	
19	export const importInto = (call, body, groupId = 'trip') => call('POST', `/groups/${groupId}/import`, body)
20	
21	export const rejected = problems => ({ error: 'import rejected', problems })
22	
23	// Runs fn({ call, file, restart }) with a running app whose data file already holds the trip group.
24	// restart() stops the app and starts a new one on the same data file; call always reaches the current app.
25	export async function withTrip(fn, group = trip) {
26	  const data = tempDataFile()
27	  let app = await startApp(data.file)
28	  try {
29	    const created = await app.call('POST', '/groups', group)
30	    assert.equal(created.status, 201)
31	    const restart = async () => {
32	      await app.stop()
33	      app = await startApp(data.file)
34	    }
35	    await fn({ call: (...args) => app.call(...args), file: data.file, restart })
36	  } finally {
37	    await app.stop()
38	    data.cleanup()
39	  }
40	}
41	
42	// What changes when the data file is written: its text, its inode (a save renames a new file over it) and mtime.
43	// Also lists the folder, so a stray temp file shows up.
44	export function snapshot(file) {
45	  const { ino, mtimeNs } = statSync(file, { bigint: true })
46	  return { text: readFileSync(file, 'utf8'), ino, mtimeNs, folder: readdirSync(dirname(file)) }
47	}
48

1	import { test } from 'node:test'
2	import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
3	import { expense, importInto, payment, snapshot, withTrip } from './import-fixtures.mjs'
4	
5	const raw = JSON.stringify
6	const one = raw([expense()])
7	const err = error => ({ error })
8	const ENTRIES_MSG = 'entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items'
9	
10	// Every reply so far saved nothing: same data file and empty lists.
11	async function assertNothingSaved({ call, file }, before) {
12	  assert.deepEqual(snapshot(file), before)
13	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/expenses')).body, { expenses: [] })
14	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/payments')).body, { payments: [] })
15	}
16	
17	// The next expense still gets id 1.
18	async function assertNextExpenseIsOne(call) {
19	  const next = await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', { description: 'Hotel', payer: 'Ann', amount: 90 })
20	  assert.equal(next.status, 201)
21	  assert.equal(next.body.id, 1)
22	}
23	
24	// Sends each body to the import route and checks the exact status and error body.
25	async function expectAll(ctx, bodies, status, expected, groupId = 'trip') {
26	  const before = snapshot(ctx.file)
27	  for (const body of bodies) {
28	    const r = await importInto(ctx.call, body, groupId)
29	    assert.equal(r.status, status, String(raw(body)))
30	    assert.deepEqual(r.body, expected(body), String(raw(body)))
31	  }
32	  await assertNothingSaved(ctx, before)
33	}

35	test('a body over 10 KB is 413, before the group check, and saves nothing', () => withTrip(async ctx => {
36	  const big = { entries: [expense({ description: 'x'.repeat(11 * 1024) })] }
37	  await expectAll(ctx, [big], 413, () => err('body too large'))
38	  await expectAll(ctx, [big], 413, () => err('body too large'), 'nope')
39	}))

41	test('a body that is not a JSON object is 400, before the group check', () => withTrip(async ctx => {
42	  for (const groupId of ['trip', 'nope']) {
43	    await expectAll(ctx, ['[]', 'null', '"x"', '5', 'true'], 400, () => err('body must be a JSON object'), groupId)
44	    await expectAll(ctx, ['{'], 400, () => err('invalid JSON'), groupId)
45	  }
46	}))

48	test('an unknown group wins over every later check', () => withTrip(async ctx => {

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.
